title: Why Is Amer Sports, Inc. (AS) Stock Up +9.55% Today?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
# Key Takeaways

* [AS](https://tickeron.com/ticker/AS/) shares jumped 9.55%, or $2.78, to $31.88 in Tuesday morning trade, extending the advance after gapping higher at the open.
* The primary catalyst was a better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter report, with revenue up 24% and adjusted earnings comfortably ahead of consensus.
* Management raised full-year revenue, margin and EPS guidance, and the board authorized a $1 billion share repurchase program.
* Secondary drivers included heavy volume, a rebound from five consecutive down sessions, and modest strength in athletic footwear peers.
* Broader context was mixed: the S&P 500 proxy slipped about 0.2% while consumer discretionary lagged modestly, making the move almost entirely stock-specific.
* **News Significance Score: 68/100** — Major earnings and guidance beat met a move nearly five times the stock's typical daily swing.
* Traders are watching whether the stock can hold the $31 area into the close and how much of the buyback is executed before year-end.

# Amer Sports Beats and Raises, Sparking a Sharp Rebound

Amer Sports, Inc. ([AS](https://tickeron.com/ticker/AS/)) is the New York-listed sporting goods group behind Arc'teryx, Salomon, Wilson, Peak Performance and Atomic, with more than $6.6 billion in annual revenue. The stock rose 9.55% to $31.88 on Tuesday morning, up from Monday's close of $29.10, after the company reported third-quarter results and lifted its full-year outlook before the opening bell. The direction is unambiguously higher and the size of the move places it among the stock's largest single-session gains of the past quarter. The immediate reason cited by the market: an earnings and guidance beat, sweetened by a new $1 billion buyback authorization.

# Q3 Results: Growth Beat on Every Line

The company reported revenue of $2.169 billion for the quarter ended September 30, up 24% year over year and 23% in constant currency, ahead of expectations near $2.14 billion. Adjusted diluted earnings per share came in at $0.42, well above the consensus in the high-20s to mid-30s cent range, while adjusted net income rose 35% to $250 million and adjusted operating profit climbed 30% to $357 million.

Margins expanded in tandem. Adjusted gross margin widened 150 basis points to 59.4%, helped by favorable channel, regional and product mix and less off-price discounting, while adjusted operating margin rose 70 basis points to 16.4%. Net income attributable to shareholders rose 67% to $239.6 million, or $0.41 per diluted share.

* Technical Apparel revenue rose 26% to $861 million, with Arc'teryx posting a 16% omni-channel comparable gain.
* Outdoor Performance revenue climbed 27% to $917 million on Salomon softgoods demand.
* Ball & Racquet revenue grew 12% to $391 million, though segment margin contracted 210 basis points to 6.1%.
* Direct-to-consumer sales jumped 36% and now represent roughly 45% of revenue.
* Asia-Pacific ex-China grew 48%, Greater China 30%, the Americas 22% and EMEA 10%.

# Raised Guidance and a $1 Billion Buyback

Management now expects fiscal 2026 revenue growth of approximately 25% to 26%, up from about 24%, and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.32 to $1.35 versus a prior $1.27 to $1.30 range. The adjusted operating margin target moved to 14.5%–14.7% from 14.2%–14.5%. An initial 2027 framework points to revenue growth in the low double digits to mid-teens, the midpoint of the company's long-term algorithm.

The board also authorized a $1 billion share repurchase program with no expiration, and the company intends to buy back up to $200 million of stock before December 31. With $594 million of net cash at quarter-end, that capital return carries no balance-sheet strain and amplifies the per-share earnings effect of the raise. The combination of an operating beat, a higher bar for the fourth quarter and a fresh buyback is exactly the package that forces short-term positioning to unwind.

# A Rebound From a Five-Session Slide

The reaction was magnified by the setup. The stock had fallen in each of the previous five sessions, sliding from $32.46 on November 9 to $29.10 on Monday, a decline of more than 10% that left it near the lower end of its two-month range. Momentum funds and short-horizon traders were positioned defensively into the print, and Tuesday's open near $30.40 forced that positioning to reverse quickly. Shares are still below the late-October high of $32.83, so the move reads as a sharp repricing of expectations rather than a breakout to new highs.

# Market Context and Trading Activity

Volume was heavy. Roughly 2 million shares changed hands in the first 30 minutes of trading, a pace well above the stock's three-month average of about 6.7 million shares per full session; Monday's turnover of 13.3 million shares was already double the norm ahead of the release. Athletic footwear peers participated only modestly: [NKE](https://tickeron.com/ticker/NKE/) rose 2.67%, [LULU](https://tickeron.com/ticker/LULU/) gained 2.01%, [ONON](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ONON/) added 1.07% and [DECK](https://tickeron.com/ticker/DECK/) advanced 0.80%, while the broad market slipped about 0.2% and the consumer discretionary sector was roughly flat. The divergence confirms the move was driven by company fundamentals, not sector sympathy. Technically, the gap reclaimed the $30 support shelf that had capped the stock in early November and pushed it back above its 50-day moving average.

# News Significance Score

The score runs from 0, meaning no meaningful news and a move that is normal for the stock, to 100, meaning transformative news and an extreme, rare price move. Amer Sports earns 68 out of 100.

The verified news was major rather than routine: a double-digit revenue beat, an earnings beat, raised full-year guidance and a new $1 billion buyback, all material relative to a company valued near $18 billion. The price response was also unusually large. The stock's average absolute daily move over the past 60 sessions is roughly 1.9%, and today's gain is close to five times that figure. No session in that stretch produced a move of comparable size. Strong fundamental news and a rare, outsized reaction combine into a high-but-not-extreme score.

# What Comes Next for Amer Sports

The next scheduled update is fourth-quarter and full-year fiscal 2026 results. Investors will focus on whether holiday sell-through at Arc'teryx and Salomon sustains the 36% direct-to-consumer growth rate, and whether inventory, up 16% to $1.98 billion, converts cleanly into cash. Greater China, at roughly 30% of sales, remains the key macro variable, and any softening there would test the revised guidance. Watch also the pace of the buyback and commentary on freight, fuel surcharges and tariff costs that are pressuring gross margin, along with the Ball & Racquet segment's 6.1% margin. Wall Street carried a Strong Buy consensus into the print, with 26 of 27 analysts rating the shares a buy, so the burden is now on execution rather than sentiment. Risks include a decelerating premium outdoor market, currency headwinds in EMEA and elevated valuation near 31 times trailing earnings.
